subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee a persistent plain-text TUI mode covering both OpenClaw and pi-tui-rendered interface glyphs, and what ASCII vocabulary should it use?
rationale: The accessibility need and affected code paths are clear, but the activation mechanism, substitution vocabulary, Markdown scope, and dependency ownership become durable user-facing product contracts.

options.title: Guarantee full plain-text mode
options.body: Add one documented `tui` accessibility setting and cover all relevant OpenClaw and pi-tui interface glyphs, contributing upstream configuration seams where needed.

options.title: Limit to OpenClaw chrome
options.body: Replace only OpenClaw-owned decorations and explicitly document that pi-tui Markdown rendering may still contain Unicode, accepting a partial mode.

options.title: Decline the mode
options.body: Keep current rendering and rely on external terminal or screen-reader workarounds rather than providing a supported accessibility contract.

recommendation.title: Guarantee full plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Add one documented `tui` accessibility setting and cover all relevant OpenClaw and pi-tui interface glyphs, contributing upstream configuration seams where needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and the sampled feature history point most strongly to ownership of the central TUI and tool-display implementation.
